verification_operation: Inspect the official Apache Kafka 4.2.0 Admin-client ListTransactions request-construction and protocol-schema source family to determine whether an empty producer-ID filter is rewritten, omitted, or retained before transport.

sources.observation: buildBatchedRequest always calls request.setProducerIdFilters(new ArrayList<>(options.filteredProducerIds())) with no non-empty guard; an empty options set therefore becomes an empty ProducerIdFilters collection in ListTransactionsRequestData before the request builder is returned.
ProducerIdFilters is a []int64 field present in versions 0+; the schema states that if it is empty, all transactions are returned, while non-empty values filter by producer ID.

finding_summary: In Apache Kafka 4.2.0, the Admin-client ListTransactionsHandler does not repair an empty producer-ID filter into match-none or suppress it at request construction: it unconditionally places options.filteredProducerIds() into ListTransactionsRequestData, so an empty set becomes an empty protocol-field collection. The 4.2.0 protocol schema defines that empty ProducerIdFilters means no producer-ID filtering. This carries FE-512's empty-as-unfiltered contract through request construction, but this slice did not inspect generated serializer bytes or live broker behavior.
falsifying_trace: Input at this layer: options.filteredProducerIds() is empty.
Handler constructs ListTransactionsRequestData and unconditionally invokes setProducerIdFilters(new ArrayList<>(emptySet)).
Protocol schema defines ProducerIdFilters for all request versions 0+ and assigns empty the meaning 'all transactions'.
Therefore there is no handler-level conversion from empty to match-none before the request builder; the exact byte representation and broker execution remain unverified in this slice.

No claim about generated serialization byte layout, broker-side decoding/execution, authorization, later client-side filtering, Flink runtime reachability, or any Kafka/Flink version outside the pinned sources.
